headline: Oct 29: HSC and equivalent results to be published
summary: The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee has announced the date for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate results.
details: The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on October 29, according to the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee.
Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chairman of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka, confirmed the decision during a meeting with the education minister and secretary.
Further details regarding the publication of the results will be announced on October 26.
Students across the country are now awaiting the final outcome of their college-level examinations.

headline_marked: Police find [[primary evidence of sexual abuse]] of 7-year-old girl at Tongi madrasah
headline: Police find primary evidence of sexual abuse of 7-year-old girl at Tongi madrasah
summary: A madrasah teacher has been arrested following allegations of abuse. Police have collected CCTV footage and recorded the child's statement in court.
details: Police have found primary evidence of the sexual abuse of a seven-year-old girl at a madrasah in Tongi, Gazipur. A 30-year-old teacher, Moslem Ahmed, Ahmed has been arrested and is currently in jail.

The incident allegedly occurred on October 19, on the stairs of the madrasah's ground floor. The child's family discovered the abuse after she initially refused to go to the المدرسة (madrasah) and later revealed the details to her parents.

Following the discovery, the child's family members went to the madrasah on October 21, where they confronted the accused teacher. This led to a confrontation where the teacher was beaten by a crowd of local people.

The madrasah's founder and principal, Almas Hossain, has filed a separate complaint alleging that a group of 15-16 people led by the child's father beat the other teachers and security guards, vandalized the office, and looted 17 lakh BDT and five mobile phones.

The child's father has denied the allegations of looting and vandalism, stating he only went to the madrasah to seek justice for his daughter. He has requested a fair trial and security for his family.
Police have since visited the scene, collected CCTV footage and other evidence, and {// a 30-year-old teacher has been arrested} recorded the child's statement before a magistrate court.
